positive_results: 5 of 8 preregistered unseen tasks are clean autonomous wins
v4 has a 3-task-win and 37.5 percentage-point success-rate advantage over the restricted v3-compatible architecture
human task-specific solver contribution remained zero by frozen provenance records
negative_results: v4 has zero task-win margin over random search
v4 has zero task-win margin over template synthesis
v4 has zero task-win margin over the no-transfer ablation
Task 7 exposes a numerical-safety failure mode in the broader mechanism vocabulary
causal_conclusion: The evidence supports broader non-v3 mechanism availability as the source of the three v4-over-v3 task wins. It rejects learned cross-domain transfer and transfer-weighted ranking as the cause of improved generalization.
external_validation_status: G8 protocol prepared; independent external execution remains optional for validating the partial claims but cannot convert the failed preregistered transfer/baseline gates into a v4 breakthrough.
final_v4_claim: Lexigen v4 is a useful autonomous unseen-task optimization/discovery system with demonstrable breadth and a real improvement over its restricted predecessor, accompanied by a negative result for its stronger transfer-learning thesis. It is not a world-level AI breakthrough.
next_scientific_action: Freeze v4 permanently and create a new preregistered successor architecture where transferred learned mechanisms are causally distinct from no-transfer and simpler baseline arms before selecting fresh untouched holdouts.
